authorization: The user asks for imaginative candidate meanings for the remaining signs, following Bonta's recommendations and choosing working interpretations on the balance of available evidence.
objective: Give every observed non-editorial Wells code and every additional directly mapped catalogue code a ranked working interpretation. Preserve Bonta's proposed values as inherited hypotheses and supply new semantic and lexical candidates for the rest.
new_inputs: The retained manuscript now has glyph crops and a first-coder candidate crosswalk. The task also expands from six anchor roles to the full graphic inventory. This permits new hypothesis construction; previous lexical construction-set results are not rerun as validation.
assumptions: Bonta's early Indo-Aryan and mixed logographic/phonetic interpretation is the working scenario for this exercise.
A sign can function as a lexical sign, sound component, measure or field marker in different contexts. A sound component need not have its own word meaning.
Known Bonta values are provisional anchors. Direct many-to-many catalogue candidates remain alternatives; no transitive allograph merge is applied.
Pictorial resemblance supplies candidate senses. It is combined with observed position, neighbours, numeral adjacency and repeated contexts.

Modifiers such as enclosures, repetition, internal ticks and added plant/implement components generate administrative, quantitative or compound hypotheses. Their proposed effects are explicitly speculative.

Dictionary matches constrain candidate sounds under this scenario. Modern dictionary attestation supplies vocabulary, not Bronze Age dating. Classical and later names remain possible comparison forms, not authenticated historical readings.
procedure: Pin every input by SHA256. Read only observational fields from the derivative corpus.
Construct aggregate sign dossiers, retaining whole-corpus coverage and a separate complete single-line reading-order frame. Count unique sequences and distinct object families separately.
Import the manuscript's proposed sign variants through its candidate graphic crosswalk. Preserve alternatives and source confidence.

Search two- and three-sign windows with one unknown against Monier-Williams headwords, first exactly and then with an explicit Bonta-like normalization. Rank candidate residual sounds by the distinct lexical contexts they satisfy; retain conflicts and alternatives.
Compute preceding/following context similarity and positional distributions. Use these to propose roles and related semantic families.
Choose preferred semantic hypotheses from the inspected shapes, functional context and lexical candidates. Give alternatives and distinguish specific lexical proposals from broad role proposals.
Publish a local reviewable catalogue, selected worked examples, source manifest, construction outputs, and a retrospective. Do not overwrite any earlier endpoint.
ranking: Ordinal preferences: inherited anchor, supported working candidate, tentative working candidate, or minimal-evidence placeholder. These are uncalibrated judgments within the assumed scenario, not numerical posterior probabilities.
stopping: Complete coverage of the declared graphic inventory, an explicit preferred interpretation and alternatives for each code, an automated anchor-based lexical pass, and checked links to the observations and sources used. Weakly evidenced codes can have broad semantic-role assignments; lack of a specific lexeme stays visible.
storage: Acquired material, complete context strings and full lexical-search outputs remain under data/raw/2026-10-08-bonta-extension/. Original analysis code, aggregate dossiers and project-authored candidate interpretations are retained in the dated experiment directory.
validation_scope: Check coverage, input integrity, category counts, crosswalk bounds, dictionary match reconstruction and output links. This is a construction exercise, not an independent decipherment evaluation.
